clue.text: Irrational fear may be seen in sinister pout

indicators.note: the answer may be seen once the letters of the two words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's sinister pout betrays an irrational fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be seen in' is the anagram signal: the twelve letters of SINISTER POUT rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstition is an irrational belief, often a dread of omens such as black cats or broken mirrors.

clue.text: Pay out to retain us — or deal thus with payment if broke?

definitions.text: deal thus with payment if broke

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so the word for paying out wraps round the next piece

parts.note: to pay out money is to spend it

explanation.surface: Someone told to pay out for us wonders whether to stop paying when broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' means hold inside. A firm that is broke may stop paying its debts for a while, and the clue's 'thus' points back at that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that runs out of money may halt, or put off, its payments for a time.

clue.text: Top of prison twice used for demonstration!

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter in a down clue

parts.note: the top of a building is its roof

explanation.surface: The top of a prison is used twice to make a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice used' tells you that 'Top' works two ways: as 'Top of' it picks P from 'prison', and on its own it means ROOF.
explanation.definitionFit: A proof is a demonstration that something is true.

clue.text: Bird touching bread put out on street

parts.note: re means about or concerning, i.e. touching on

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or displaced, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird touches bread that someone has put out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' turns BREAD into DBREA; 'touching' reads like a sentimental adjective but is the short word for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is commonly called a redbreast after its orange-red chest.

clue.text: Tour to rush along, missing nothing

indicators.note: missing means the letter for nothing is left out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
to rip is to move along at great speed
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A tour goes by in a rush, missing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: TO RIP loses its O to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey or excursion, like a tour.

clue.text: Islander will get brown going around Haiti possibly

indicators.note: going around means the word for brown surrounds the other letters

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: possibly says the word Haiti is only one possible order of its letters

explanation.surface: An islander gets a tan travelling around Haiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges HAITI to AHITI, and 'going around' puts TAN about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Pacific island of Tahiti is an islander.

clue.text: Dyke builder has left refuse

parts.note: Offa, the eighth-century king of Mercia, built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border

explanation.surface: The builder of an embankment has left behind some rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFA'S DYKE is an earthwork along the England–Wales border, named after the Mercian king Offa.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal can mean waste or rubbish as well as edible animal innards.

clue.text: Colours afresh material with bad stain

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of stain are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recolours fabric that has a bad stain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges STAIN to AINTS after REP, a ribbed fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaint is to put new colour on again, coating something afresh.

clue.text: Business alliance allowed Rex and Bill to get turnover

indicators.note: turnover here means the whole string of letters is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: let means allowed
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A firm's alliance let Rex and Bill take a share of the turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like business income but signals that LET + R + AC is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartel is a group of firms acting together to fix prices or limit competition.

clue.text: Sea-going cutter?

parts.note: a cutter suggests a sailing boat, but this cutter is a fish whose snout is a long blade

explanation.definitionFit: This ocean fish has a long sword-like bill that it slashes with, a cutter that lives at sea.

clue.text: Female left-winger accepted by soccer authority

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside the following body

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A socialist is admitted to the governing body of football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts one piece inside the other; 'left-winger' sounds like a footballer but is a political term, apt beside soccer.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a woman's name, so a female.

clue.text: Use some beef for this

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook is told to use some beef for this dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort and use both mean exertion, as in 'put some use into it'.

clue.text: Strong supporter

explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means sturdy and strong as an adjective, and as a noun a loyal, reliable supporter.

clue.text: Hell can bring this!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and so the underworld itself
may means can, be able or allowed to

explanation.surface: Hell can bring this!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: hell would cause consternation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is alarm and distress, what the prospect of hell would bring.

clue.text: Start of summer leading to nudity or revealing wear

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: undress is the state of having few or no clothes on

explanation.surface: The start of summer brings nudity or revealing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundress is a light dress that leaves shoulders and arms bare for hot weather.

clue.text: Having political divisions — the fashion in Panama perhaps?

indicators.note: in means placed inside the waterway

parts.note: the Panama Canal is an example of a canal
le ton is French for fashionable style, so ton is the fashion

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what is in fashion in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the old word for high fashion inside the waterway; 'Panama' looks like a country or a hat but is its canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Countries such as Switzerland are split into cantons, so cantonal means relating to such districts.

clue.text: Read out story with quiet ending

indicators.note: read out means the words are heard, so we go by how they sound

parts.note: a story is a tale and quiet is peace

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a story that has a peaceful ending.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE and PEACE said one after the other sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a final section or decoration added at the end of something.

clue.text: Jacks start to cheer their leading vessel

parts.note: a jack is a flag flown at a ship's bow
hip is the opening call of 'hip, hip, hooray'

explanation.surface: Sailors on the flagship cheer as the jacks go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to cheer' looks like a first-letter pick, but it means HIP, how the cheer begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagship is the ship carrying the admiral, which leads a fleet.

clue.text: Where to have a pint after Choral Evensong naturally?

parts.note: a pub or inn is where one has a pint
choral evensong is famously sung at Ely Cathedral, so after it one is at Ely

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where to have a beer after evensong.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as INN AT ELY: a pub in the cathedral city of Ely, in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something innately means doing it by inborn nature.

clue.text: Let fags do their worst? It's fashionable to get healthy!

parts.note: in means fashionable
hale means healthy

explanation.surface: Smoking is now trendy and supposedly good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fags' is British slang for cigarettes; the definition is cryptic, taking smoke into the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing cigarette smoke into the lungs is how a smoker lets the cigarettes do harm.

clue.text: American beauty queen is a married woman

parts.note: a beauty contest winner takes the title Miss

explanation.surface: Miss America turns out to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS US reads as an American beauty queen, though the title is really Miss America.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is an informal word for a wife.

clue.text: Little people should be shut up — right little devils!

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
imps are small devils

explanation.surface: Small children ought to be quiet, the little devils.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrimps is an informal term for tiny people.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is slang for a very small person, so shrimps are diminutive folk.

clue.text: Their strange period establishing historical tradition

indicators.note: strange means the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Their odd era set up a custom handed down through history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges THEIR to HERIT before AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what is inherited from the past, such as customs and buildings.

clue.text: Trunk can come out of roots

indicators.note: the answer can come out of the word roots by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A tree trunk grows up out of its roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can come out of' rearranges ROOTS; 'Trunk' looks like part of a tree but is the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is the human body without head or limbs, its trunk.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly goes back in the bath on return?

indicators.note: on return means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to redip is to dip in again

explanation.surface: Something creepy keeps coming back to the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: REDIPS read backwards gives the answer, a creature well known for turning up in baths.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is an eight-legged creature often called a creepy-crawly.

clue.text: One who deduces God's existence from the swirling tides?

indicators.note: swirling means the letters of tides are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone infers a creator from the movement of the tides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges TIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: A deist believes in a creator on the evidence of reason and nature rather than revelation.

clue.text: What's in Palm Sunday's collection for distribution on Maundy Thursday?

definitions.text: collection for distribution on Maundy Thursday

indicators.note: What's in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The question is what goes into the church collection over Holy Week.
explanation.walkthrough: On Maundy Thursday the British monarch gives out special coins to the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Maundy money is given as charity, gifts to the poor.

clue.text: Letters selected initially as a source of enlightenment

definitions.text: Letters selected initially as a source of enlightenment

parts.words: Letters selected initially as a source of enlightenment
parts.note: the name is built from the initials of a scientific phrase, and it makes light

explanation.definitionFit: The device's name is an acronym for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation, and it emits a beam of light.

clue.text: Greek character, girl, is received, by royal personage

indicators.note: received means taken in by the following piece

parts.note: HM is short for His or Her Majesty
Ellen is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek character and a girl are received by a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: ELLEN and IS go inside HM, His or Her Majesty; 'Greek character' suggests a letter like alpha.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellenism is Greek culture and spirit, the national character of the Greeks.

clue.text: Remark about Post Office beginning to slip is not daft

indicators.note: about means surrounding the following letters

parts.note: a comment is a remark

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about the post office starting to slip is sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the remark round the Post Office and S, which 'beginning to' takes from 'slip'.
explanation.definitionFit: Compos mentis is Latin for of sound mind, the opposite of daft.
